Title:
Fix for mobile wallet discovery + "memorynet"

Description:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above --> ## Description <!--- Describe your changes in detail --> The DHT did not propagate private discovery messages to wallets because they do not have the `MESSAGE_PROPAGATION` feature. This PR changes the behaviour of the DHT to include wallets in discovery propagation messages. Internally, the Forward step of the DHT pipeline has a special case that will propagate to wallets. The closest peer selection has been adjusted to allow the caller to specify the PeerFeatures of the closest nodes to target by using the `neighbours_with_features` call. _NOTE:_ because those nodes will not propagate the message further, the selection ensures that a minimum number of propagation nodes are always selected This PR also includes a new example called "memorynet". `memorynet`, as the name suggests, is a small in-memory DHT network consisting of a number of "base nodes" and "wallets" (all that differs is their feature flags). The following happens when running `memorynet`: 1. A single "seed node", `NUM_NODES` "base nodes" and `NUM_WALLETS` "wallets" are generated and started. 1. All "base nodes" join the network via the "seed node" 1. All "wallets" join the network via a random "base node" 1. The first "wallet" in the list attempts to discover the last "wallet" in the list 1. The result of the discovery is printed and the network is shut down The example can be run with this command: `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 RUST_LOG=trace cargo run --example memorynet 2> /tmp/debug.log` ## Motivation and Context <!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? --> <!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. --> Closes #1204 The _memorynet_ example provides clean and easy to read output that allows you to easily see what is happening between a network of nodes. Each generated node is assigned a name that is used in stdout output. Normal internal logs are logged to stderr and can be switched on using the `RUST_LOG` environment variable. ```text ---------------------------------------------------------- Bringing up virtual network consisting of a seed node, 15 nodes and 2 wallets ---------------------------------------------------------- Node 'Bob' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' Node 'Carol' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' Node 'Charlie' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Charlie (d4eaac42550edbd9)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Charlie (d4eaac42550edbd9)' EVENT: 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' connected to 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' EVENT: 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' got inbound connection from 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' (snip...) ---------------------------------------------------------- Discovery is done. ---------------------------------------------------------- ⚡️🎉😎 'Vanna' discovered peer 'Plod (7bb7b1d55953e391)' ([7bb7b1d55953e391] PK=88aed2306b39d4c4659b6a41d98199c5a8acb48155ba1e2fa6c356edece7c251 Features=NONE | COMMUNICATION_CLIENT) in 11014ms (snip...) ``` ## How Has This Been Tested? <!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. --> <!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to --> <!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. --> _memorynet_ is a test of these changes. ## Types of changes <!--- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: --> * [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) * [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) * [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) * [x] Feature refactor (No new feature or functional changes, but performance or technical debt improvements) * [x] New Tests * [ ] Documentation ## Checklist: <!--- Go over all the following points, and put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. --> * [x] I'm merging against the `development` branch. * [x] I ran `cargo-fmt --all` before pushing. * [x] I have squashed my commits into a single commit. * [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. * [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. * [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.

Title:
[Bug]: InvalidRequestException: Each network interface requires a device index.

Description:
### Welcome to Amazon SSP EKS Accelerator! - [X] Yes, I've searched similar issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-eks-accelerator-for-terraform/issues) and didn't find any. ### Amazon EKS Accelerator Release version 1.21 ### What is your environment, configuration and the example used? ```hcl terraform { required_version = ">= 1.1.7" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = ">= 4.6.0" } kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = ">= 2.8.0" } helm = { source = "hashicorp/helm" version = ">= 2.4.1" } } backend "local" { path = "local_tf_state/terraform-main.tfstate" } } ``` ### What did you do and What did you see instead? Try to use bottlerocket ARM managed node group ```hcl terraform { required_version = ">= 1.1.7" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = ">= 4.6.0" } kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = ">= 2.8.0" } helm = { source = "hashicorp/helm" version = ">= 2.4.1" } } backend "local" { path = "local_tf_state/terraform-main.tfstate" } } data "aws_region" "current" {} data "aws_availability_zones" "available" {} data "aws_eks_cluster" "cluster" { name = module.eks-ssp.eks_cluster_id } data "aws_eks_cluster_auth" "cluster" { name = module.eks-ssp.eks_cluster_id } provider "aws" { profile = "cluster-sandbox" region = "us-west-2" } [Truncated] ```shell The first managed node work group works, but the custom one with launch template got errors: ╷ │ Error: error creating EKS Node Group (salesrise-sandbox-dev-eks:btl-arm20220323050436112600000006): InvalidRequestException: Each network interface requires a device index. │ { │ RespMetadata: { │ StatusCode: 400, │ RequestID: "eb560489-96f8-4663-86f3-6f96eea9c7a4" │ }, │ Message_: "Each network interface requires a device index." │ } │ │ with module.eks-ssp.module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups["bottlerocket_arm"].aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng, │ on .terraform/modules/eks-ssp/modules/aws-eks-managed-node-groups/main.tf line 1, in resource "aws_eks_node_group" "managed_ng": │ 1: resource "aws_eks_node_group" "managed_ng" { │ ``` ```

Comments:
- encountered same issue.
- And I found that it only failed when `create_launch_template = true`, if I removed `create_launch_template = true` or use `create_launch_template = false`, the managed group could created successful. I think there must be some bug in creating launch template.
- Thanks for reporting this issue. We have noticed this issue few days ago when `terraform-aws-provider` released a new version `4.6.0` which introduced a breaking change for launch templates. Workaround is to set the provider version to `4.5.0` in your examples. However this issue has PR has been fixed merged now. See this issue for more details https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/23766/ ```hcl aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "4.5.0" } ``` Try again and let us know if you still hit the same issue
- Hello, just some clarification in case someone else (noob like me) stumbles upon the same issue. If your case is that your terraform script broke in a half-complete state due to the template thing, chances are you are going to follow @username_2 instructions above and then proceed to hit `terraform init -upgrade` and then `terraform apply` to pick up where you left off. Personally I kept receiving the same error, and the reason was due to the fact that since I already had a state that I was trying to continue from, Terraform would find the existing launch template (that had initially failed) and continue using that. The problem is that, that template had already a problematic index. So it was a no go. The solution is to either do `terraform destroy` and start from scratch (thus creating a new template in the process) **OR** going to your AWS console: EC2 > Launch Templates , find your template created by Terraform and delete it. Then proceed with `terraform apply`. Admittedly you will have messed with cloud resources our of Terraform scope but it's a minor thing and since Terraform is awesome it can detect it and proceed without issue (again by recreating the template with the correct index). Thanks guys for your support! :-)
- @username_3 I think the later option BUT using Terraform. You can update the node group by making `create_launch_template = false` and re enable it again. I haven't tried this myself but this should work
- @username_2 Thank you, it works.

Summary:
Allow other ways to use confluence.cluster.interface on Windows

Description:
h3. Summary +As a+ system admin on Windows +I want to+ be able to set network interface parameter {{confluence.cluster.interface}} on a fixed way +So that I can+ not use the name generated by Java and use one that is fixed on Windows instead h3. Problem Definition Customers report that the network interface name (for example, _eth0_) changes by itself on Windows, sometimes, on reboot. That is not a consistent behavior and cannot be reproduced. In this case, it changed form _eth6_ to _eth7_ and caused Synchrony to fail due to Hazelcast not finding it: {code} Hazelcast CANNOT start on this node. No matching network interface found.\nInterface matching must be either disabled or updated in the hazelcast.xml config file. {code} More information: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58632235/get-name-of-a-specific-network-interface-in-java http://hg.openjdk.java.net/jdk8/jdk8/jdk/file/82b276590b85/src/windows/native/java/net/NetworkInterface.c#l172 {quote} * Windows does not have any standard for device names so we are forced * to use our own convention which is based on the normal Unix naming * convention ("lo" for the loopback, eth0, eth1, .. for ethernet devices, * tr0, tr1, .. for token ring, and so on). This convention gives us * consistency across multiple Windows editions and also consistency with * Solaris/Linux device names. Note that we always enumerate in index * order and this ensures consistent device number across invocations. */ {quote} h3. Workaround Use the instruction on this kb, whenever that behavior is observed: [Hazelcast CANNOT start on this node. Title:
Fix for mobile wallet discovery + "memorynet"

Description:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above --> ## Description <!--- Describe your changes in detail --> The DHT did not propagate private discovery messages to wallets because they do not have the `MESSAGE_PROPAGATION` feature. This PR changes the behaviour of the DHT to include wallets in discovery propagation messages. Internally, the Forward step of the DHT pipeline has a special case that will propagate to wallets. The closest peer selection has been adjusted to allow the caller to specify the PeerFeatures of the closest nodes to target by using the `neighbours_with_features` call. _NOTE:_ because those nodes will not propagate the message further, the selection ensures that a minimum number of propagation nodes are always selected This PR also includes a new example called "memorynet". `memorynet`, as the name suggests, is a small in-memory DHT network consisting of a number of "base nodes" and "wallets" (all that differs is their feature flags). The following happens when running `memorynet`: 1. A single "seed node", `NUM_NODES` "base nodes" and `NUM_WALLETS` "wallets" are generated and started. 1. All "base nodes" join the network via the "seed node" 1. All "wallets" join the network via a random "base node" 1. The first "wallet" in the list attempts to discover the last "wallet" in the list 1. The result of the discovery is printed and the network is shut down The example can be run with this command: `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 RUST_LOG=trace cargo run --example memorynet 2> /tmp/debug.log` ## Motivation and Context <!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? --> <!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. --> Closes #1204 The _memorynet_ example provides clean and easy to read output that allows you to easily see what is happening between a network of nodes. Each generated node is assigned a name that is used in stdout output. Normal internal logs are logged to stderr and can be switched on using the `RUST_LOG` environment variable. ```text ---------------------------------------------------------- Bringing up virtual network consisting of a seed node, 15 nodes and 2 wallets ---------------------------------------------------------- Node 'Bob' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' Node 'Carol' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' Node 'Charlie' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Charlie (d4eaac42550edbd9)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Charlie (d4eaac42550edbd9)' EVENT: 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' connected to 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' EVENT: 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' got inbound connection from 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' (snip...) ---------------------------------------------------------- Discovery is done. ---------------------------------------------------------- ⚡️🎉😎 'Vanna' discovered peer 'Plod (7bb7b1d55953e391)' ([7bb7b1d55953e391] PK=88aed2306b39d4c4659b6a41d98199c5a8acb48155ba1e2fa6c356edece7c251 Features=NONE | COMMUNICATION_CLIENT) in 11014ms (snip...) ``` ## How Has This Been Tested? <!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. --> <!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to --> <!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. --> _memorynet_ is a test of these changes. ## Types of changes <!--- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: --> * [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) * [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) * [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) * [x] Feature refactor (No new feature or functional changes, but performance or technical debt improvements) * [x] New Tests * [ ] Documentation ## Checklist: <!--- Go over all the following points, and put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. --> * [x] I'm merging against the `development` branch. * [x] I ran `cargo-fmt --all` before pushing. * [x] I have squashed my commits into a single commit. * [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. * [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. * [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.

Title:
[Bug]: InvalidRequestException: Each network interface requires a device index.

Description:
### Welcome to Amazon SSP EKS Accelerator! - [X] Yes, I've searched similar issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-eks-accelerator-for-terraform/issues) and didn't find any. ### Amazon EKS Accelerator Release version 1.21 ### What is your environment, configuration and the example used? ```hcl terraform { required_version = ">= 1.1.7" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = ">= 4.6.0" } kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = ">= 2.8.0" } helm = { source = "hashicorp/helm" version = ">= 2.4.1" } } backend "local" { path = "local_tf_state/terraform-main.tfstate" } } ``` ### What did you do and What did you see instead? Try to use bottlerocket ARM managed node group ```hcl terraform { required_version = ">= 1.1.7" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = ">= 4.6.0" } kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = ">= 2.8.0" } helm = { source = "hashicorp/helm" version = ">= 2.4.1" } } backend "local" { path = "local_tf_state/terraform-main.tfstate" } } data "aws_region" "current" {} data "aws_availability_zones" "available" {} data "aws_eks_cluster" "cluster" { name = module.eks-ssp.eks_cluster_id } data "aws_eks_cluster_auth" "cluster" { name = module.eks-ssp.eks_cluster_id } provider "aws" { profile = "cluster-sandbox" region = "us-west-2" } [Truncated] ```shell The first managed node work group works, but the custom one with launch template got errors: ╷ │ Error: error creating EKS Node Group (salesrise-sandbox-dev-eks:btl-arm20220323050436112600000006): InvalidRequestException: Each network interface requires a device index. │ { │ RespMetadata: { │ StatusCode: 400, │ RequestID: "eb560489-96f8-4663-86f3-6f96eea9c7a4" │ }, │ Message_: "Each network interface requires a device index." │ } │ │ with module.eks-ssp.module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups["bottlerocket_arm"].aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng, │ on .terraform/modules/eks-ssp/modules/aws-eks-managed-node-groups/main.tf line 1, in resource "aws_eks_node_group" "managed_ng": │ 1: resource "aws_eks_node_group" "managed_ng" { │ ``` ```

Comments:
- encountered same issue.
- And I found that it only failed when `create_launch_template = true`, if I removed `create_launch_template = true` or use `create_launch_template = false`, the managed group could created successful. I think there must be some bug in creating launch template.
- Thanks for reporting this issue. We have noticed this issue few days ago when `terraform-aws-provider` released a new version `4.6.0` which introduced a breaking change for launch templates. Workaround is to set the provider version to `4.5.0` in your examples. However this issue has PR has been fixed merged now. See this issue for more details https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/23766/ ```hcl aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "4.5.0" } ``` Try again and let us know if you still hit the same issue
- Hello, just some clarification in case someone else (noob like me) stumbles upon the same issue. If your case is that your terraform script broke in a half-complete state due to the template thing, chances are you are going to follow @username_2 instructions above and then proceed to hit `terraform init -upgrade` and then `terraform apply` to pick up where you left off. Personally I kept receiving the same error, and the reason was due to the fact that since I already had a state that I was trying to continue from, Terraform would find the existing launch template (that had initially failed) and continue using that. The problem is that, that template had already a problematic index. So it was a no go. The solution is to either do `terraform destroy` and start from scratch (thus creating a new template in the process) **OR** going to your AWS console: EC2 > Launch Templates , find your template created by Terraform and delete it. Then proceed with `terraform apply`. Admittedly you will have messed with cloud resources our of Terraform scope but it's a minor thing and since Terraform is awesome it can detect it and proceed without issue (again by recreating the template with the correct index). Thanks guys for your support! :-)
- @username_3 I think the later option BUT using Terraform. You can update the node group by making `create_launch_template = false` and re enable it again. I haven't tried this myself but this should work
- @username_2 Thank you, it works.

Description:
h3. Summary +As a+ system admin on Windows +I want to+ be able to set network interface parameter {{confluence.cluster.interface}} on a fixed way +So that I can+ not use the name generated by Java and use one that is fixed on Windows instead h3. That is not a consistent behavior and cannot be reproduced. This convention gives us * consistency across multiple Windows editions and also consistency with * Solaris/Linux device names. Title:
Fix for mobile wallet discovery + "memorynet"

Description:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above --> ## Description <!--- Describe your changes in detail --> The DHT did not propagate private discovery messages to wallets because they do not have the `MESSAGE_PROPAGATION` feature. This PR changes the behaviour of the DHT to include wallets in discovery propagation messages. Internally, the Forward step of the DHT pipeline has a special case that will propagate to wallets. The closest peer selection has been adjusted to allow the caller to specify the PeerFeatures of the closest nodes to target by using the `neighbours_with_features` call. _NOTE:_ because those nodes will not propagate the message further, the selection ensures that a minimum number of propagation nodes are always selected This PR also includes a new example called "memorynet". `memorynet`, as the name suggests, is a small in-memory DHT network consisting of a number of "base nodes" and "wallets" (all that differs is their feature flags). The following happens when running `memorynet`: 1. A single "seed node", `NUM_NODES` "base nodes" and `NUM_WALLETS` "wallets" are generated and started. 1. All "base nodes" join the network via the "seed node" 1. All "wallets" join the network via a random "base node" 1. The first "wallet" in the list attempts to discover the last "wallet" in the list 1. The result of the discovery is printed and the network is shut down The example can be run with this command: `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 RUST_LOG=trace cargo run --example memorynet 2> /tmp/debug.log` ## Motivation and Context <!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? --> <!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. --> Closes #1204 The _memorynet_ example provides clean and easy to read output that allows you to easily see what is happening between a network of nodes. Each generated node is assigned a name that is used in stdout output. Normal internal logs are logged to stderr and can be switched on using the `RUST_LOG` environment variable. ```text ---------------------------------------------------------- Bringing up virtual network consisting of a seed node, 15 nodes and 2 wallets ---------------------------------------------------------- Node 'Bob' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' Node 'Carol' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' Node 'Charlie' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Charlie (d4eaac42550edbd9)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Charlie (d4eaac42550edbd9)' EVENT: 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' connected to 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' EVENT: 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' got inbound connection from 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' (snip...) ---------------------------------------------------------- Discovery is done. ---------------------------------------------------------- ⚡️🎉😎 'Vanna' discovered peer 'Plod (7bb7b1d55953e391)' ([7bb7b1d55953e391] PK=88aed2306b39d4c4659b6a41d98199c5a8acb48155ba1e2fa6c356edece7c251 Features=NONE | COMMUNICATION_CLIENT) in 11014ms (snip...) ``` ## How Has This Been Tested? <!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. --> <!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to --> <!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. --> _memorynet_ is a test of these changes. ## Types of changes <!--- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: --> * [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) * [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) * [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) * [x] Feature refactor (No new feature or functional changes, but performance or technical debt improvements) * [x] New Tests * [ ] Documentation ## Checklist: <!--- Go over all the following points, and put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. --> * [x] I'm merging against the `development` branch. * [x] I ran `cargo-fmt --all` before pushing. * [x] I have squashed my commits into a single commit. * [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. * [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. * [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.

Title:
Error if keyword substitution yields empty result

Description:
This is PR #153 except rebased to and to be applied to `develop` rather than `feature/grpc`. Comments from the previous PR include that we may need some regression testing before merging. (Description from previous PR follows.) When the command_reference config_get_token and config_set methods use keyword-based parameter substitution, array elements that contain a parameter not supplied by the caller will be omitted from the result array. This behavior is desired to support, e.g., CLI interaction involving VRFs, where both the presence or absence of a VRF are permissible and should result in CLI interaction either containing or not containing a vrf statement. However, this behavior makes it easy for developer oversight or typo to result in an empty command line (which is bad). This commit updates command_reference so that if the result of keyword-based parameter substitution is an empty array then an ArgumentError will be raised. It also adds new assertions to test this behavior to the existing test_config_get_token_hash_substitution test case, and updates the documentation and changelog.

Description:
### Welcome to Amazon SSP EKS Accelerator! - [X] Yes, I've searched similar issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-eks-accelerator-for-terraform/issues) and didn't find any. ### Amazon EKS Accelerator Release version 1.21 ### What is your environment, configuration and the example used? ```hcl terraform { required_version = ">= 1.1.7" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = ">= 4.6.0" } kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = ">= 2.8.0" } helm = { source = "hashicorp/helm" version = ">= 2.4.1" } } backend "local" { path = "local_tf_state/terraform-main.tfstate" } } ``` ### What did you do and What did you see instead? Try to use bottlerocket ARM managed node group ```hcl terraform { required_version = ">= 1.1.7" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = ">= 4.6.0" } kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = ">= 2.8.0" } helm = { source = "hashicorp/helm" version = ">= 2.4.1" } } backend "local" { path = "local_tf_state/terraform-main.tfstate" } } data "aws_region" "current" {} data "aws_availability_zones" "available" {} data "aws_eks_cluster" "cluster" { name = module.eks-ssp.eks_cluster_id } data "aws_eks_cluster_auth" "cluster" { name = module.eks-ssp.eks_cluster_id } provider "aws" { profile = "cluster-sandbox" region = "us-west-2" } [Truncated] ```shell The first managed node work group works, but the custom one with launch template got errors: ╷ │ Error: error creating EKS Node Group (salesrise-sandbox-dev-eks:btl-arm20220323050436112600000006): InvalidRequestException: Each network interface requires a device index. │ { │ RespMetadata: { │ StatusCode: 400, │ RequestID: "eb560489-96f8-4663-86f3-6f96eea9c7a4" │ }, │ Message_: "Each network interface requires a device index." │ } │ │ with module.eks-ssp.module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups["bottlerocket_arm"].aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng, │ on .terraform/modules/eks-ssp/modules/aws-eks-managed-node-groups/main.tf line 1, in resource "aws_eks_node_group" "managed_ng": │ 1: resource "aws_eks_node_group" "managed_ng" { │ ``` ```

Comments:
- encountered same issue.
- And I found that it only failed when `create_launch_template = true`, if I removed `create_launch_template = true` or use `create_launch_template = false`, the managed group could created successful. I think there must be some bug in creating launch template.
- Thanks for reporting this issue. We have noticed this issue few days ago when `terraform-aws-provider` released a new version `4.6.0` which introduced a breaking change for launch templates. Workaround is to set the provider version to `4.5.0` in your examples. However this issue has PR has been fixed merged now. See this issue for more details https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/23766/ ```hcl aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "4.5.0" } ``` Try again and let us know if you still hit the same issue
- Hello, just some clarification in case someone else (noob like me) stumbles upon the same issue. If your case is that your terraform script broke in a half-complete state due to the template thing, chances are you are going to follow @username_2 instructions above and then proceed to hit `terraform init -upgrade` and then `terraform apply` to pick up where you left off. Personally I kept receiving the same error, and the reason was due to the fact that since I already had a state that I was trying to continue from, Terraform would find the existing launch template (that had initially failed) and continue using that. The problem is that, that template had already a problematic index. So it was a no go. The solution is to either do `terraform destroy` and start from scratch (thus creating a new template in the process) **OR** going to your AWS console: EC2 > Launch Templates , find your template created by Terraform and delete it. Then proceed with `terraform apply`. Admittedly you will have messed with cloud resources our of Terraform scope but it's a minor thing and since Terraform is awesome it can detect it and proceed without issue (again by recreating the template with the correct index). Thanks guys for your support! :-)
- @username_3 I think the later option BUT using Terraform. You can update the node group by making `create_launch_template = false` and re enable it again. I haven't tried this myself but this should work
- @username_2 Thank you, it works.

This convention gives us * consistency across multiple Windows editions and also consistency with * Solaris/Linux device names. Title:
Fix for mobile wallet discovery + "memorynet"

Description:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above --> ## Description <!--- Describe your changes in detail --> The DHT did not propagate private discovery messages to wallets because they do not have the `MESSAGE_PROPAGATION` feature. This PR changes the behaviour of the DHT to include wallets in discovery propagation messages. Internally, the Forward step of the DHT pipeline has a special case that will propagate to wallets. The closest peer selection has been adjusted to allow the caller to specify the PeerFeatures of the closest nodes to target by using the `neighbours_with_features` call. _NOTE:_ because those nodes will not propagate the message further, the selection ensures that a minimum number of propagation nodes are always selected This PR also includes a new example called "memorynet". `memorynet`, as the name suggests, is a small in-memory DHT network consisting of a number of "base nodes" and "wallets" (all that differs is their feature flags). The following happens when running `memorynet`: 1. A single "seed node", `NUM_NODES` "base nodes" and `NUM_WALLETS` "wallets" are generated and started. 1. All "base nodes" join the network via the "seed node" 1. All "wallets" join the network via a random "base node" 1. The first "wallet" in the list attempts to discover the last "wallet" in the list 1. The result of the discovery is printed and the network is shut down The example can be run with this command: `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 RUST_LOG=trace cargo run --example memorynet 2> /tmp/debug.log` ## Motivation and Context <!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? --> <!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. --> Closes #1204 The _memorynet_ example provides clean and easy to read output that allows you to easily see what is happening between a network of nodes. Each generated node is assigned a name that is used in stdout output. Normal internal logs are logged to stderr and can be switched on using the `RUST_LOG` environment variable. ```text ---------------------------------------------------------- Bringing up virtual network consisting of a seed node, 15 nodes and 2 wallets ---------------------------------------------------------- Node 'Bob' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' Node 'Carol' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' Node 'Charlie' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Charlie (d4eaac42550edbd9)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Charlie (d4eaac42550edbd9)' EVENT: 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' connected to 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' EVENT: 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' got inbound connection from 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' (snip...) ---------------------------------------------------------- Discovery is done. ---------------------------------------------------------- ⚡️🎉😎 'Vanna' discovered peer 'Plod (7bb7b1d55953e391)' ([7bb7b1d55953e391] PK=88aed2306b39d4c4659b6a41d98199c5a8acb48155ba1e2fa6c356edece7c251 Features=NONE | COMMUNICATION_CLIENT) in 11014ms (snip...) ``` ## How Has This Been Tested? <!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. --> <!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to --> <!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. --> _memorynet_ is a test of these changes. ## Types of changes <!--- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: --> * [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) * [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) * [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) * [x] Feature refactor (No new feature or functional changes, but performance or technical debt improvements) * [x] New Tests * [ ] Documentation ## Checklist: <!--- Go over all the following points, and put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. --> * [x] I'm merging against the `development` branch. * [x] I ran `cargo-fmt --all` before pushing. * [x] I have squashed my commits into a single commit. * [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. * [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. * [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.

Title:
[Bug]: InvalidRequestException: Each network interface requires a device index.

Description:
### Welcome to Amazon SSP EKS Accelerator! - [X] Yes, I've searched similar issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-eks-accelerator-for-terraform/issues) and didn't find any. ### Amazon EKS Accelerator Release version 1.21 ### What is your environment, configuration and the example used? ```hcl terraform { required_version = ">= 1.1.7" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = ">= 4.6.0" } kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = ">= 2.8.0" } helm = { source = "hashicorp/helm" version = ">= 2.4.1" } } backend "local" { path = "local_tf_state/terraform-main.tfstate" } } ``` ### What did you do and What did you see instead? Try to use bottlerocket ARM managed node group ```hcl terraform { required_version = ">= 1.1.7" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = ">= 4.6.0" } kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = ">= 2.8.0" } helm = { source = "hashicorp/helm" version = ">= 2.4.1" } } backend "local" { path = "local_tf_state/terraform-main.tfstate" } } data "aws_region" "current" {} data "aws_availability_zones" "available" {} data "aws_eks_cluster" "cluster" { name = module.eks-ssp.eks_cluster_id } data "aws_eks_cluster_auth" "cluster" { name = module.eks-ssp.eks_cluster_id } provider "aws" { profile = "cluster-sandbox" region = "us-west-2" } [Truncated] ```shell The first managed node work group works, but the custom one with launch template got errors: ╷ │ Error: error creating EKS Node Group (salesrise-sandbox-dev-eks:btl-arm20220323050436112600000006): InvalidRequestException: Each network interface requires a device index. │ { │ RespMetadata: { │ StatusCode: 400, │ RequestID: "eb560489-96f8-4663-86f3-6f96eea9c7a4" │ }, │ Message_: "Each network interface requires a device index." │ } │ │ with module.eks-ssp.module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups["bottlerocket_arm"].aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng, │ on .terraform/modules/eks-ssp/modules/aws-eks-managed-node-groups/main.tf line 1, in resource "aws_eks_node_group" "managed_ng": │ 1: resource "aws_eks_node_group" "managed_ng" { │ ``` ```

Comments:
- encountered same issue.
- And I found that it only failed when `create_launch_template = true`, if I removed `create_launch_template = true` or use `create_launch_template = false`, the managed group could created successful. I think there must be some bug in creating launch template.
- Thanks for reporting this issue. We have noticed this issue few days ago when `terraform-aws-provider` released a new version `4.6.0` which introduced a breaking change for launch templates. Workaround is to set the provider version to `4.5.0` in your examples. However this issue has PR has been fixed merged now. See this issue for more details https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/23766/ ```hcl aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "4.5.0" } ``` Try again and let us know if you still hit the same issue
- Hello, just some clarification in case someone else (noob like me) stumbles upon the same issue. If your case is that your terraform script broke in a half-complete state due to the template thing, chances are you are going to follow @username_2 instructions above and then proceed to hit `terraform init -upgrade` and then `terraform apply` to pick up where you left off. Personally I kept receiving the same error, and the reason was due to the fact that since I already had a state that I was trying to continue from, Terraform would find the existing launch template (that had initially failed) and continue using that. The problem is that, that template had already a problematic index. So it was a no go. The solution is to either do `terraform destroy` and start from scratch (thus creating a new template in the process) **OR** going to your AWS console: EC2 > Launch Templates , find your template created by Terraform and delete it. Then proceed with `terraform apply`. Admittedly you will have messed with cloud resources our of Terraform scope but it's a minor thing and since Terraform is awesome it can detect it and proceed without issue (again by recreating the template with the correct index). Thanks guys for your support! :-)
- @username_3 I think the later option BUT using Terraform. You can update the node group by making `create_launch_template = false` and re enable it again. I haven't tried this myself but this should work
- @username_2 Thank you, it works.

Description:
h3. Summary +As a+ system admin on Windows +I want to+ be able to set network interface parameter {{confluence.cluster.interface}} on a fixed way +So that I can+ not use the name generated by Java and use one that is fixed on Windows instead h3. This convention gives us * consistency across multiple Windows editions and also consistency with * Solaris/Linux device names. Title:
Fix for mobile wallet discovery + "memorynet"

Description:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above --> ## Description <!--- Describe your changes in detail --> The DHT did not propagate private discovery messages to wallets because they do not have the `MESSAGE_PROPAGATION` feature. This PR changes the behaviour of the DHT to include wallets in discovery propagation messages. Internally, the Forward step of the DHT pipeline has a special case that will propagate to wallets. The closest peer selection has been adjusted to allow the caller to specify the PeerFeatures of the closest nodes to target by using the `neighbours_with_features` call. _NOTE:_ because those nodes will not propagate the message further, the selection ensures that a minimum number of propagation nodes are always selected This PR also includes a new example called "memorynet". `memorynet`, as the name suggests, is a small in-memory DHT network consisting of a number of "base nodes" and "wallets" (all that differs is their feature flags). The following happens when running `memorynet`: 1. A single "seed node", `NUM_NODES` "base nodes" and `NUM_WALLETS` "wallets" are generated and started. 1. All "base nodes" join the network via the "seed node" 1. All "wallets" join the network via a random "base node" 1. The first "wallet" in the list attempts to discover the last "wallet" in the list 1. The result of the discovery is printed and the network is shut down The example can be run with this command: `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 RUST_LOG=trace cargo run --example memorynet 2> /tmp/debug.log` ## Motivation and Context <!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? --> <!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. --> Closes #1204 The _memorynet_ example provides clean and easy to read output that allows you to easily see what is happening between a network of nodes. Each generated node is assigned a name that is used in stdout output. Normal internal logs are logged to stderr and can be switched on using the `RUST_LOG` environment variable. ```text ---------------------------------------------------------- Bringing up virtual network consisting of a seed node, 15 nodes and 2 wallets ---------------------------------------------------------- Node 'Bob' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' Node 'Carol' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' Node 'Charlie' is joining the network via the seed node 'Alice' EVENT: 'Charlie (d4eaac42550edbd9)' connected to 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' EVENT: 'Alice (1dc460f5fe4e3675)' got inbound connection from 'Charlie (d4eaac42550edbd9)' EVENT: 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' connected to 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' EVENT: 'Carol (dea46505688b5ac7)' got inbound connection from 'Bob (1d79bcc44d814748)' (snip...) ---------------------------------------------------------- Discovery is done. ---------------------------------------------------------- ⚡️🎉😎 'Vanna' discovered peer 'Plod (7bb7b1d55953e391)' ([7bb7b1d55953e391] PK=88aed2306b39d4c4659b6a41d98199c5a8acb48155ba1e2fa6c356edece7c251 Features=NONE | COMMUNICATION_CLIENT) in 11014ms (snip...) ``` ## How Has This Been Tested? <!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. --> <!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to --> <!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. --> _memorynet_ is a test of these changes. ## Types of changes <!--- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: --> * [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) * [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) * [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) * [x] Feature refactor (No new feature or functional changes, but performance or technical debt improvements) * [x] New Tests * [ ] Documentation ## Checklist: <!--- Go over all the following points, and put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. --> * [x] I'm merging against the `development` branch. * [x] I ran `cargo-fmt --all` before pushing. * [x] I have squashed my commits into a single commit. * [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. * [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. * [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.

Title:
[Bug]: InvalidRequestException: Each network interface requires a device index.

Description:
### Welcome to Amazon SSP EKS Accelerator! - [X] Yes, I've searched similar issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-eks-accelerator-for-terraform/issues) and didn't find any. ### Amazon EKS Accelerator Release version 1.21 ### What is your environment, configuration and the example used? ```hcl terraform { required_version = ">= 1.1.7" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = ">= 4.6.0" } kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = ">= 2.8.0" } helm = { source = "hashicorp/helm" version = ">= 2.4.1" } } backend "local" { path = "local_tf_state/terraform-main.tfstate" } } ``` ### What did you do and What did you see instead? Try to use bottlerocket ARM managed node group ```hcl terraform { required_version = ">= 1.1.7" required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = ">= 4.6.0" } kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = ">= 2.8.0" } helm = { source = "hashicorp/helm" version = ">= 2.4.1" } } backend "local" { path = "local_tf_state/terraform-main.tfstate" } } data "aws_region" "current" {} data "aws_availability_zones" "available" {} data "aws_eks_cluster" "cluster" { name = module.eks-ssp.eks_cluster_id } data "aws_eks_cluster_auth" "cluster" { name = module.eks-ssp.eks_cluster_id } provider "aws" { profile = "cluster-sandbox" region = "us-west-2" } [Truncated] ```shell The first managed node work group works, but the custom one with launch template got errors: ╷ │ Error: error creating EKS Node Group (salesrise-sandbox-dev-eks:btl-arm20220323050436112600000006): InvalidRequestException: Each network interface requires a device index. │ { │ RespMetadata: { │ StatusCode: 400, │ RequestID: "eb560489-96f8-4663-86f3-6f96eea9c7a4" │ }, │ Message_: "Each network interface requires a device index." │ } │ │ with module.eks-ssp.module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups["bottlerocket_arm"].aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng, │ on .terraform/modules/eks-ssp/modules/aws-eks-managed-node-groups/main.tf line 1, in resource "aws_eks_node_group" "managed_ng": │ 1: resource "aws_eks_node_group" "managed_ng" { │ ``` ```

Comments:
- encountered same issue.
- And I found that it only failed when `create_launch_template = true`, if I removed `create_launch_template = true` or use `create_launch_template = false`, the managed group could created successful. I think there must be some bug in creating launch template.
- Thanks for reporting this issue. We have noticed this issue few days ago when `terraform-aws-provider` released a new version `4.6.0` which introduced a breaking change for launch templates. Workaround is to set the provider version to `4.5.0` in your examples. However this issue has PR has been fixed merged now. See this issue for more details https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/23766/ ```hcl aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "4.5.0" } ``` Try again and let us know if you still hit the same issue
- Hello, just some clarification in case someone else (noob like me) stumbles upon the same issue. If your case is that your terraform script broke in a half-complete state due to the template thing, chances are you are going to follow @username_2 instructions above and then proceed to hit `terraform init -upgrade` and then `terraform apply` to pick up where you left off. Personally I kept receiving the same error, and the reason was due to the fact that since I already had a state that I was trying to continue from, Terraform would find the existing launch template (that had initially failed) and continue using that. The problem is that, that template had already a problematic index. So it was a no go. The solution is to either do `terraform destroy` and start from scratch (thus creating a new template in the process) **OR** going to your AWS console: EC2 > Launch Templates , find your template created by Terraform and delete it. Then proceed with `terraform apply`. Admittedly you will have messed with cloud resources our of Terraform scope but it's a minor thing and since Terraform is awesome it can detect it and proceed without issue (again by recreating the template with the correct index). Thanks guys for your support! :-)
- @username_3 I think the later option BUT using Terraform. You can update the node group by making `create_launch_template = false` and re enable it again. I haven't tried this myself but this should work
- @username_2 Thank you, it works.
